root_cause: In URLStrParser.parseURLBody, username and password are set ONLY from an inline 'user:password@' userinfo segment, so WHEN there is no such userinfo segment (pwdEndIdx <= 0, which is the case for a URL whose password contains '#', since line 105 truncates the decoded body at the first '#') AND the credentials are present merely as query parameters (parameters.get(USERNAME_KEY)/parameters.get(PASSWORD_KEY) non-empty), the constructed URL keeps username == null and password == null, causing URL.getUsername()/getPassword() to return null and the downstream NPE.

read vul/URLStrParser.java:44-97 -> parseDecodedStr splits the string at '?', so decodedBody excludes the query and parameters holds username/password while the body may contain no userinfo segment.
read vul/URLStrParser.java:105-108 -> poundIndex = decodedBody.indexOf('#'); the body is truncated at '#', so a password containing '#' can never survive in the userinfo position.
read vul/URLStrParser.java:137-149 -> username/password are read only from the userinfo substring; when pwdEndIdx <= 0 they stay null and there is no fallback to parameters.
read vul/URLStrParser.java:174 -> the URL is built with the null username/password even though parameters still carries USERNAME_KEY/PASSWORD_KEY.
